area: Microscopic traffic simulation realism SOTA (2024-2026): SUMO toolchain, calibrated real-city scenarios, driver heterogeneity, demand realism, Python control on Windows, determinism
benchmarks: GEH statistic on link/detector counts: GEH < 5 for >= 85% of measured links, 100% < 10 = acceptable calibration (UK DMRB/WebTAG, WSDOT, FHWA-derived guidelines; https://handwiki.org/wiki/Engineering:GEH_statistic)
Individual link flows within +/-15% of observed for >= 85% of links (UKDoT 2014 / WSDoT 2014 microsimulation guidelines)

Route travel times within +/-15% (or +/-1 minute if shorter) of floating-car/probe measurements (FHWA Traffic Analysis Toolbox Vol. III family of criteria; see also VTRC 22-R7 https://vtrc.virginia.gov/media/vtrc/vtrc-pdf/vtrc-pdf/22-R7.pdf)
RMSE / RMSNE / SQV on time-sliced detector counts and speeds across all count stations (used by InTAS: 24 stations; HaTS: 7 count sites; BeST: Berlin induction loops)

Distributional realism vs trajectory data: KS-test / Jensen-Shannon divergence on speed, time-headway, time-gap and acceleration distributions; 2024 roadside-radar calibration found DEFAULT SUMO models produce systematically shorter time headways than reality until calibrated (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/382345459)

WOSAC (Waymo Open Sim Agents Challenge) realism meta-metric [0-1], combining kinematic (speed/accel), interactive (collision, TTC, nearest-object distance) and map-based (offroad, distance-to-edge) components, plus minADE; benchmark values: SUMO 0.653 vs best learned simulator SMART 0.751 at 8 s horizon; at 60 s SUMO collision rate 0.0047 / offroad 0.0073 beats most learned models (TrafficBots v1.5: 0.2507 / 0.1526) (arXiv 2512.18537)

Fundamental diagram / MFD shape agreement — SNMF-SPSA (Transportmetrica B 2025) embeds the macroscopic fundamental diagram in the OD-calibration objective (https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/21680566.2025.2459928)

Simulation-health counters as realism red flags: SUMO teleport count, emergency-braking events, collisions, and jam-caused vehicle removals should be ~0 in a well-calibrated scenario (SUMO statistics output)

Detector-coverage validation protocol: hold out a subset of count stations from calibration and report GEH/correlation on held-out stations (done in arXiv 2606.03823 genetic calibration of Greensboro, which generalized to unseen road segments)
Daily-profile validation: 24 h simulated volume curve vs observed diurnal loop-count curve per station (LuST, TAPASCologne, BeST all validate against 24 h profiles rather than single-hour counts)
findings:
CONTEXT NOTE: this repo (SCMS-Simulator) already runs Eclipse MOSAIC + VeReMi NextGen on Windows, driving SUMO through MOSAIC's TraCI-based SumoAmbassador, and already wires InTAS urban/highway time-slice variants plus MOSAIC bundle maps (Barnim, Tiergarten, Highway) and procedural grid/spider/rand/OSM maps (scms-sim/scenarios/gen_scenario.py, docs/adr/0001-stack-and-approach.md). Findings below are selected for that stack.

== 1. Where SUMO realism stands overall (2025 benchmark) ==
"Systematic Benchmarking of SUMO Against Data-Driven Traffic Simulators" (arXiv 2512.18537, Dec 2025, https://arxiv.org/html/2512.18537v1) evaluated SUMO on the Waymo Open Sim Agents Challenge (WOSAC) against six learned simulators (SMART, BehaviorGPT, GUMP, MVTE, VBD, TrafficBots v1.5). SUMO scored 0.653 on the WOSAC realism meta-metric vs 0.751 for SMART — i.e., 86.9% of SOTA with <100 tunable parameters vs millions — and on 60 s horizons SUMO was MORE stable than learned models (collision rate 0.0047, offroad 0.0073 vs TrafficBots 0.2507/0.1526). Implication: a carefully calibrated SUMO remains a defensible SOTA substrate for city-scale V2X; the realism gap vs learned models is in short-horizon kinematic micro-behavior (accelerations, headways), which is exactly what EIDM + heterogeneous vType distributions + sublane model target.

== 2. Network realism: netconvert OSM import ==
Docs: https://sumo.dlr.de/docs/Networks/Import/OpenStreetMap.html . Known OSM import defects: dual carriageways produce doubled junctions; traffic_signals nodes mapped ahead of the real intersection; every crossing node becomes an independent TLS; missing turn lanes. Standard mitigation set: --junctions.join (default in osmBuild.py), --tls.guess-signals, --try-join-tls / --tls.join, --ramps.guess, --geometry.remove, plus typemaps (osmNetconvert*.typ.xml) and manual repair in netedit. osmWebWizard is convenience-only and does not expose the accurate-import options (https://sumo.dlr.de/docs/Tutorials/Import_from_OpenStreetMap.html). Every published calibrated city scenario (LuST, InTAS, HaTS, BeST) did substantial MANUAL network correction (lane counts, TLS programs, junction topology) in netedit — the field's consensus is that raw OSM import alone is NOT publication-grade realism; real signal plans are the single biggest manual win (InTAS encodes the 20 real deployed TLS programs of Ingolstadt).

== 3. Demand calibration toolchain (SUMO-native) ==
- routeSampler.py (since 1.5.0; https://sumo.dlr.de/docs/Tools/Turns.html and Demand/Routes_from_Observation_Points.html): samples from a candidate route set (e.g., randomTrips output) to satisfy edge counts, turn counts and/or OD relations per time interval; supports GEH-based optimization and mode-specific counts. Currently the recommended count-based method for urban nets. A SUMO UC 2024 paper (https://sumo.dlr.de/pdf/2024/1-3.pdf) shows an ILP formulation beats stock flowrouter/routeSampler fits.
- dfrouter (Demand/Routes_from_Observation_Points.html): derives flows AND routes purely from induction-loop data; works well only with dense detector coverage, i.e., motorways — used for highway scenarios, poor for urban grids.
- od2trips: converts (time-sliced) VISUM/Vissim-format OD matrices over TAZ polygons into trips — the entry point for classic 4-step/gravity-model demand.
- Calibrators (https://sumo.dlr.de/docs/Simulation/Calibrator.html): online per-edge flow/speed enforcement — insert vehicles when flow is below target, remove when above or jammed (jamThreshold default 0.5); paired with routeProbe detectors so injected vehicles get realistic route distributions. Caveat from SUMO devs: realism downstream of a calibrator depends on how well the underlying route set matches real routes (https://www.eclipse.org/lists/sumo-user/msg06322.html).
- Rerouters: mid-simulation route/destination/parking reassignment zones; used with --device.rerouting.* options for dynamic en-route rerouting (note thread caveat in §7).
- Assignment: duaIterate.py (iterative dynamic user assignment, Gawron) and marouter; TAPASCologne used Gawron DUA; LuST ships both a shortest-path+rerouting variant and a DUE variant.
- SOTA calibration research 2024-2026: SNMF-SPSA (spectral-clustering SPSA + MFD objective, Transportmetrica B 2025, https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/21680566.2025.2459928); hybrid neural real-time OD calibration under disruptions (arXiv 2408.06659); Google-scale multi-city metropolitan highway calibration (arXiv 2501.04783); genetic-algorithm calibration of a full SUMO city (Greensboro NC) from sparse counts, inferring job distributions that matched census employment and generalizing to held-out segments (arXiv 2606.03823); simulation-free flow estimation from sparse counts (arXiv 2606.23536); MG-TuRBO high-dimensional Bayesian optimization for simulator calibration (arXiv 2604.08569); dynamic real-time SUMO calibration framework (https://sumo.dlr.de/preprints/pre-print-3321.pdf).

== 4. Behavioral models ==
- Car-following: default Krauss (sigma=0.5 driver imperfection). EIDM (Extended IDM, Salles et al., SUMO Conf 2020, https://sumo.dlr.de/docs/Car-Following-Models/EIDM.html) is the designated human-like model: adds drive-off dynamics validated against aerial drone trajectories; still evolving (reaction time, spatial anticipation planned). 2024 SUMO-in-the-loop calibration with roadside-radar trajectories on a 1.5 km signalized corridor recalibrated Krauss/IDM/W99 and found default SUMO headways too short vs reality (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/382345459). 2025 MDPI paper calibrated CF+LC jointly for heterogeneous traffic (https://doi.org/10.3390/su18147025).
- Lane change: LC2013 (default) executes instantaneous lateral jumps; SL2015 + sublane model (--lateral-resolution) gives continuous lateral dynamics (maxSpeedLat, minGapLat, latAlignment, lcSublane, lcPushy, lcImpatience) and is what recent digital-twin/work-zone papers use for realistic merging (https://sumo.dlr.de/docs/Simulation/SublaneModel.html, arXiv 2508.06544). MOBIL is not a stock SUMO model (it is IDM's companion in the literature; SUMO's equivalents are LC2013/SL2015).
- Junctions (https://sumo.dlr.de/docs/Simulation/Intersections.html): internal lanes + internal junctions (waiting inside intersection), right-of-way with minor links and gap acceptance (jmTimegapMinor, jmDriveAfterRedTime, dynamic impatience growing with waiting time), zipper merges, keep-clear heuristic. Docs concede no empirical validation of junction dynamics is published — junction realism comes mostly from correct TLS programs and network geometry.
- Pedestrians (https://sumo.dlr.de/docs/Simulation/Pedestrians.html): models nonInteracting, striping (default; 2D stripes on sidewalks/crossings), and since ~1.19 a coupled JuPedSim (Julich social-force simulator) for crowd-level realism (https://sumo.dlr.de/docs/jupedsim.html).
- Perception errors: SUMO's DriverState device injects Wiener-process perception errors (speed/gap) per driver — relevant for misbehavior-detection ground truth vs honest-driver noise.

== 5. Driver heterogeneity / stochasticity ==
Per-vehicle speedFactor is drawn from a truncated normal by default ("normc(mean,dev,min,max)"; default dev 0.1 for road vehicles) — this alone creates realistic desired-speed spread (https://sumo.dlr.de/docs/Definition_of_Vehicles,_Vehicle_Types,_and_Routes.html, https://sumo.dlr.de/docs/Simulation/VehicleSpeed.html). vTypeDistribution elements plus tools/createVehTypeDistribution.py let you sample whole correlated parameter sets (accel, decel, tau, sigma, lc* params, lengths) from normal/uniform/gamma distributions per driver — the published-scenario practice for driver heterogeneity. VeReMi NextGen itself advertises "multiple driver profiles" as one of its realism additions over VeReMi/VeReMi-Extension (https://oparu.uni-ulm.de/items/a1a874b1-c15a-4f8d-9fae-082368353aaf). Randomness sources are cleanly separable: independent Mersenne-Twister streams for vehicle loading, probabilistic flows, driving dynamics and devices, all controlled by one seed (default 23423) (https://sumo.dlr.de/docs/Simulation/Randomness.html).

== 6. Calibrated real-city scenarios (what each was calibrated against) ==
- LuST (Luxembourg, Codeca/Frank/Engel VNC 2015; https://github.com/lcodeca/LuSTScenario): 24 h city scenario; demand built from real demographic/mobility data, validated against real traffic data from University of Luxembourg VehicularLab; ships DUA-with-rerouting and DUE variants. CRITICAL: generated/validated with SUMO 0.26 — on modern SUMO the mobility "cannot be considered validated"; authors point users to MoST. VeReMi and VeReMi-Extension are built on a LuST subnetwork (https://veremi-dataset.github.io/).
- TAPASCologne (https://sumo.dlr.de/docs/Data/Scenarios/TAPASCologne.html): Cologne, 400 km2, 24 h, >700k car trips; demand from the TAPAS activity-based system (German travel-habit surveys + infrastructure data from the German Federal Statistical Office), OSM network, Gawron dynamic user assignment (http://kolntrace.project.citi-lab.fr/). The canonical activity-based (not gravity/OD) large scenario.
- MoST (Monaco, Codeca & Harri 2017/18; https://github.com/lcodeca/MoSTScenario): 3D (elevation) multimodal C-ITS playground — cars, PT, vulnerable road users; the maintained successor to LuST.
- InTAS (Ingolstadt, Lobo et al. SUMO Conf 2020; arXiv 2011.11995, https://github.com/silaslobo/InTAS): manually corrected network with buildings; 20 TLS with the REAL deployed signal programs; demand via activitygen from demographic data + real-traffic info; buses per real timetables; validated against 24 real measurement points. A TUM variant exists (https://github.com/TUM-VT/sumo_ingolstadt). Already integrated in this repo via VeReMi NextGen.
- BeST (Berlin, 2023, https://github.com/mosaic-addons/best-scenario, https://eclipse.dev/mosaic/post/best-scenario-short/): 24 h, ~2.25M motorized-private trips, calibrated against real induction-loop data, and explicitly MOSAIC-compatible (same stack as this project); 2025 follow-up adds modeled bus traffic (Fraunhofer FOKUS, https://publica.fraunhofer.de/entities/publication/e26e598e-5539-445e-a299-c23ca681e7ef).
- HaTS (Hannover, Bosch Research, SUMO Conf 2024; https://www.tib-op.org/ojs/index.php/scp/article/view/2605, https://github.com/boschresearch/HanoverTrafficScenario): 06:00-19:00 vehicles + high-density bicycle traffic, network/TLS refined for the city center, flows from 7 real intersection counts.
- Bologna (COLOMBO/iTETRIS; https://github.com/DLR-TS/sumo-scenarios/tree/main/bologna/): small district ("Ringway"), validated with navigation-service open data.
- TuST (Turin, https://github.com/marcorapelli/TuSTScenario): 600 km2, mesoscopic. (The "Manhattan" name in SUMO circles is the synthetic Manhattan-grid mobility model, not a calibrated NYC scenario.)
- Highway/V2X-relevant: Alicante-Murcia 97 km freeway, 9 full days calibrated from Spanish road authority (DGT) data (https://github.com/msepulcre/Alicante-Murcia-SUMO-Scenario); Stuttgart STOMP motorway (Bosch, https://github.com/boschresearch/stuttgart-sumo-traffic-scenario); Geneva motorway digital twin DT-GM driven by real-time counters (https://github.com/SiLab-group/DigitalTwin_GenevaMotorway); DLR germany-motorways mesoscopic. Full index: https://sumo.dlr.de/docs/Data/Scenarios.html (also ETH 24 h scenarios for Boston/Lisbon/LA/Rio/SF and a Toronto open-data multimodal net).

== 7. Demand paradigms: gravity/OD vs activity-based ==
Time-sliced OD matrices (od2trips) remain the workhorse where cities publish OD data, but the realism SOTA is activity-based: TAPAS (used for TAPASCologne), MATSim (co-evolutionary utility-maximizing daily plans per agent; retains person-level consistency that OD matrices destroy — delays propagate through an agent's day; https://sumo.dlr.de/docs/Demand/Activity-based_Demand_Generation.html, https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2666691X25000296), SUMO's own activitygen (simple statistics-based), and SAGA (SUMO Activity GenerAtion, Codeca & Erdmann, SUMO Conf 2020; https://github.com/lcodeca/SUMOActivityGen): builds a multimodal activity-based scenario directly from an OSM extract (buildings, parking, PT) with iterative refinement hooks — the fastest route to "activity-based demand for an arbitrary city". MATSim-SUMO/MOSAIC couplings exist for large-scale multi-layer runs.

== 8. TraCI vs libsumo on Windows; MOSAIC specifics ==
libsumo embeds SUMO in-process with the same API as TraCI; measured ~10x less overhead than socket TraCI (LibSignal, arXiv 2211.10649); `pip install libsumo` works on Windows; limitations: sumo-gui unusable on Windows, no multiple clients, some context-subscription limits, stricter typing; since 1.16 Windows needs library preloading (Simulation.preloadLibraries() wraps it since 1.24) (https://sumo.dlr.de/docs/Libsumo.html). IMPORTANT FOR THIS REPO: Eclipse MOSAIC's SumoAmbassador speaks socket TraCI by design — libsumo is only relevant for standalone Python calibration/analysis loops outside MOSAIC. MOSAIC passes `--seed 100000` to SUMO by default (CSumo config) and has its own scenario-level randomSeed for mapping — both must be varied together for replications (https://eclipse.dev/mosaic/docs/simulators/traffic_simulator_sumo/).

== 9. Determinism ==
SUMO with fixed seed, fixed inputs and single-threaded execution is deterministic and generally reproducible across platforms (https://sumo.dlr.de/docs/Simulation/Randomness.html). Documented exceptions: (a) --threads N makes results non-deterministic run-to-run; (b) --device.rerouting.threads combined with random weights; (c) EIDM and DriverState use log() whose libm results differ across platforms; (d) proj-library geo-transforms differ across proj versions/platforms (affects network building, so build networks once and version them, not per-run). TraCI itself does not break determinism if the client issues identical commands in identical order. SUMO releases relevant to 2024-2026: 1.23 (May 2025), 1.24 (Jul 2025), 1.25 (Nov 2025) (https://sumo.dlr.de/docs/ChangeLog.html); pin the version — scenario validation is version-bound (LuST/0.26 precedent).

tools.name: routeSampler.py (SUMO)
tools.what: Builds demand by sampling candidate routes to match real edge counts, turn counts, and OD relations per time interval; supports GEH-target optimization
tools.maturity: Mature, actively developed since SUMO 1.5; recommended count-calibration path
tools.windows_feasibility: Full (ships in SUMO tools/, pure Python)
tools.integration_effort: Low-medium: needs a candidate route set (randomTrips/duarouter) + count data files

tools.name: dfrouter (SUMO)
tools.what: Derives flows and routes purely from induction-loop detector data; motorway-grade only
tools.integration_effort: Low for highway scenarios with dense detectors; unsuitable for urban grids

tools.name: od2trips + duaIterate.py (SUMO)
tools.what: Time-sliced OD matrices over TAZs to trips, plus iterative dynamic user assignment (Gawron) to equilibrium routes
tools.integration_effort: Medium: needs OD data and TAZ polygons; duaIterate is compute-heavy

tools.name: Calibrators + routeProbe (SUMO runtime objects)
tools.what: Online per-edge flow/speed enforcement matching detector data during the run; routeProbe supplies realistic routes for injected vehicles
tools.integration_effort: Low (additional-file XML), but realism depends on quality of underlying route distribution

tools.name: SAGA (SUMOActivityGen)
tools.what: Activity-based multimodal scenario generator directly from an OSM extract (buildings, parking, PT, activity chains), with iterative refinement
tools.maturity: Research-grade but maintained; in SUMO contributed tools
tools.integration_effort: Medium: one command to first scenario, iterations to make it credible

tools.name: EIDM car-following model (SUMO)
tools.what: Extended IDM for human-like dynamics (drive-off validated vs drone trajectories); set per vType
tools.maturity: In active development; usable, planned reaction-time/anticipation features pending
tools.windows_feasibility: Full, but log()-based math is a documented cross-platform reproducibility caveat

tools.name: SL2015 sublane model (SUMO)
tools.what: Continuous lateral dynamics and gradual lane changes (lcSublane/lcPushy/latAlignment); required for realistic merging and lateral behavior
tools.integration_effort: Low config (--lateral-resolution) but ~2-5x runtime cost and re-tuning of LC params

tools.name: vTypeDistribution + createVehTypeDistribution.py
tools.what: Per-driver heterogeneity: samples correlated vType parameter sets (speedFactor, accel, tau, sigma, lc*) from configured distributions

tools.name: JuPedSim coupling (SUMO pedestrian model)
tools.what: Social-force pedestrian dynamics from Julich coupled into SUMO (alternative to default striping model)
tools.integration_effort: Medium; only worth it if VRU realism matters to the dataset

tools.name: InTAS scenario (Ingolstadt)
tools.what: Calibrated city scenario: real TLS programs (20 junctions), activitygen demand, bus timetables, validated vs 24 count stations; already wired into this repo via VeReMi NextGen

tools.name: BeST scenario (Berlin)
tools.what: 24 h, ~2.25M trips calibrated vs real induction loops; explicitly Eclipse-MOSAIC-compatible; 2025 bus-traffic extension
tools.integration_effort: Low-medium for this repo: same MOSAIC scenario format as bundled maps; large (needs scaling/clipping for per-vehicle V2X runs)

tools.name: LuST scenario (Luxembourg)
tools.what: Classic 24 h validated city scenario underlying VeReMi/VeReMi-Extension
tools.maturity: Frozen; validated only on SUMO 0.26 — authors recommend MoST on modern SUMO
tools.integration_effort: Low, but validation claim does not transfer to current SUMO versions — cite with that caveat

tools.name: MoST scenario (Monaco)
tools.what: 3D multimodal C-ITS scenario (elevation, VRUs, PT); maintained successor to LuST

tools.name: Alicante-Murcia freeway scenario
tools.what: 97 km freeway, 9 full days, calibrated from Spanish road-authority data — strongest open highway-V2X realism
tools.integration_effort: Medium (convert to MOSAIC scenario like InTAS was)

tools.name: libsumo (pip)
tools.what: In-process SUMO with TraCI-identical API, ~10x less control overhead; for standalone Python calibration/eval loops
tools.windows_feasibility: pip install libsumo works; no sumo-gui on Windows; needs preloadLibraries since 1.16 (wrapped in 1.24)

tools.what: Agent-based activity-plan co-evolution for demand realism (person-consistent daily plans, delay propagation across trips); couple to SUMO/MOSAIC for micro-level

recommendations: 1. Anchor headline datasets on published calibrated scenarios, not procedural maps: keep the InTAS time-slice variants (already wired) as the urban core, and add the BeST Berlin scenario — it is the only large loop-calibrated scenario that is natively Eclipse-MOSAIC-compatible (mosaic-addons/best-scenario), so integration cost in gen_scenario.py is the lowest of any option; use Alicante-Murcia (9 days of road-authority-calibrated freeway) for the highway attack scenarios instead of the synthetic MOSAIC Highway bundle.

2. Add per-driver heterogeneity to every scenario run: vTypeDistribution with truncated-normal speedFactor (normc) plus createVehTypeDistribution.py-sampled accel/tau/sigma/lc parameters, and distinct vClasses (car/truck/bus shares from scenario data). This is cheap, massively improves plausibility of position/speed traces in the emitted V2X messages, and matches VeReMi NextGen's own 'driver profiles' direction.

3. Build an automated realism report emitted alongside each dataset (fits DATASHEET.md): GEH per count location (target >=85% GEH<5), link flows within +/-15% for >=85% of measured links, JSD/KS of speed and time-headway distributions vs the scenario's reference data, plus SUMO health counters (teleports, emergency stops, collisions ~ 0). This turns the 'almost identical to a real city' claim into audited numbers.

4. For any custom-OSM city (osm_ keys in mapgen), adopt the published-scenario pipeline: netconvert with --junctions.join --tls.guess-signals --tls.join --ramps.guess --geometry.remove, manual netedit repair of key junctions, real signal plans where obtainable, then routeSampler.py against city open-data counts with time-of-day intervals (optionally the ILP variant from SUMO UC 2024); use SAGA when you want activity-based multimodal demand without an OD matrix.

5. Upgrade micro-behavior selectively: EIDM vTypes for human-like car-following and SL2015 sublane for merging-critical scenarios (highway attacks, work zones) — but benchmark runtime (sublane costs several x) and note EIDM's documented cross-platform reproducibility caveat before making it the default in a determinism-audited pipeline.

6. Determinism policy: pin the SUMO version per released dataset (scenario validation is version-bound — LuST is the cautionary tale), run SUMO single-threaded (no --threads, no --device.rerouting.threads), set both MOSAIC's scenario randomSeed and the SUMO --seed (MOSAIC default 100000) explicitly from your dataset seed, and version pre-built .net.xml files rather than rebuilding (proj-version differences change networks).

7. Control-plane choice: stay on TraCI inside MOSAIC (mandatory), but use pip libsumo for standalone Python calibration/eval loops (routeSampler iteration, realism-metric computation, headless parameter sweeps) — same API, ~10x faster stepping, Windows-supported (headless only).

8. Demand time realism: prefer the scenarios' native 24 h diurnal demand (InTAS/BeST curves) sliced to windows, over constant target-flow injection; where you must synthesize, use time-sliced OD via od2trips or routeSampler interval counts so arrival rates follow the real diurnal profile rather than a homogeneous Poisson process.

9. Track (not adopt yet) learned sim-agents: WOSAC-style realism meta-metrics are the emerging cross-simulator yardstick (SUMO 0.653 vs SMART 0.751), and a WOSAC-inspired kinematic-realism score computed on your emitted BSM traces would be a novel, publishable realism claim for a misbehavior dataset.
